title: The Tower of Babel
summary: The Tower of Babel is a short lesson with one main thread: Pride says we can live without God, but God is still Lord over every nation. When you want attention so badly that you stop listening, this story reminds you that pride can scatter what people are trying to build.

read_it.prompt: Read Genesis 11:1-9. Notice one detail that would help a kid explain The Tower of Babel to someone else.

tell_it: The builders wanted a name for themselves more than they wanted to listen to God. The people tried to build a tower to make a name for themselves. God confused their language and scattered them. The pressure in the scene helps the lesson feel real.
understand_it: Kids can understand The Tower of Babel by asking what was at stake, what God revealed, and what response was faithful. Pride says we can live without God, but God is still Lord over every nation.
age_5_7_explanation: The builders wanted a name for themselves more than they wanted to listen to God.
age_8_11_explanation: The people tried to build a tower to make a name for themselves. God confused their language and scattered them. Kids can practice retelling it with the beginning, hard moment, and God-centered ending.
teen_explanation: Pride says we can live without God, but God is still Lord over every nation. A teen discussion can press into why the story mattered then and how the same truth can reshape choices now.
key_truths: Pride says we can live without God, but God is still Lord over every nation.
The Tower of Babel shows pride through a real Bible moment, not a slogan.
When you want attention so badly that you stop listening, this story reminds you that pride can scatter what people are trying to build.
life_application: When you want attention so badly that you stop listening, this story reminds you that pride can scatter what people are trying to build.

choices: To make a name for themselves
quiz_questions.answer: To make a name for themselves
quiz_questions.explanation: To make a name for themselves is the story detail to remember. The bigger lesson grows out of that detail instead of floating away from the passage.

quiz_questions.question: What is one wise response to The Tower of Babel?
quiz_questions.answer: When you want attention so badly that you stop listening, this story reminds you that pride can scatter what people are trying to build.
quiz_questions.explanation: The lesson should move from hearing to response. Pride says we can live without God, but God is still Lord over every nation.

memory_verse.prompt: Memorize or repeat Genesis 11:4 as the Bible handle for this lesson.

discussion_questions: Who needed help, courage, correction, or mercy in The Tower of Babel?
What truth should a kid remember after reading The Tower of Babel?

activity.title: Pride Tower Test
activity.instructions: Stack blocks or cups, naming one humble choice on each level before the tower gets too high.

prayer_prompt: Lord, use The Tower of Babel to teach my heart, not just my memory. Help me take one faithful next step after reading The Tower of Babel.
